raw_title: The best early October Prime Day deals happening now
title: The best early October Prime Day deals happening now
raw_summary: It’s not even October yet and Amazon is already offering some Prime Big Deal Day discounts on its own hardware, along with plenty of other popular products. It’s all to hype up October Prime Day , which starts October 6th at 3AM ET and lasts through 3AM ET on the 8th if you’re on the East Coast (12AM PT). October Prime Day offers a glimpse of deals that will likely be available again during Black Friday and Cyber Monday. So, with the holiday shopping season officially underway, you can get some of your shopping out of the way before things get busier as we approach the holidays. The most recent update to this post on October 4th was a big one. There are several deals from Apple and Beats, plus Kindle-related ones from Amazon, to name a few. Previously, we added a couple of Bose speakers and Belkin charging products. This post will be updated ahead of October 6th as new deals become available. Belkin Charging Case Pro While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better. Where to Buy: $99.99 $80.74 at Amazon (sand) $99.99 $84.99 at Belkin (sand) Nex Playground The Nex Playground is a motion-controlled console that connects to your TV and uses a built-in camera and AI to track your movements as you play. Designed for ages five and up, it comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe . You can download more games, including titles featuring popular characters like Elmo, with a paid Play Pass subscription. Where to Buy: $299 $239 at Amazon $299 $239 at Walmart $299 $239 at Best Buy Kindle Scribe Colorsoft The Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is Amazon’s first note-taking e-reader with a color screen. It features an 11-inch display, a slimmer design, an improved interface, an updated stylus, and a new AI-powered search feature that can quickly summarize documents. Where to Buy: $629.99 $479.99 at Amazon (32GB) $629.99 $479.99 at Best Buy (32GB) $679.99 $519.99 at Amazon (64GB) Kindle Scribe 32GB The third-gen Kindle Scribe 32GB is even bigger than its 10.2-inch predecessor; it offers an 11-inch display with 300ppi resolution and the same great battery life that Kindles are known for. Where to Buy: $499.99 $379.99 at Amazon $499.99 $379.99 at Best Buy iPad Mini (2024) The seventh-gen iPad Mini comes with Apple’s A17 Pro chip and support for Apple Intelligence. It’s also compatible with the Apple Pencil Pro and offers faster Wi-Fi and USB-C speeds. Read our review . Where to Buy: $599 $499 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi) $599 $449 at Best Buy (128GB, Wi-Fi) $699 $599 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi) Apple 13-inch MacBook Air (M5) Powered by Apple’s new M5 chip, the latest MacBook Airs are more powerful than prior models and offer double the base storage (512GB). They also support faster wireless standards, specifically Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Read our review . Where to Buy: $1299 $1099 at Amazon $1299 $1099 at Best Buy Apple MacBook Air (15-inch, M5, 2026) The 15-inch version of the M5 MacBook Air has better speakers and a slightly better GPU than the base 13-inch model. Where to Buy: $1499 $1299 at Amazon $1499 $1299 at Best Buy $1499 at B&H Photo Beats Studio Pro Despite the familiar design, there were plenty of upgrades in the latest Studio Pro, including noise cancellation, transparency mode, and lossless USB-C audio. Here’s our review . Where to Buy: $349.99 $149.95 at Amazon $349.99 $219.95 at Walmart $349.99 $149.99 at Best Buy Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review . Where to Buy: $249 $179.95 at Amazon $249 $224.95 at Walmart $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy Beats Powerbeats Fit A new version of the Fit Pro wireless earbuds, which are upgraded with a redesigned wing tip that Beats says is 20 percent more flexible, a smaller case, and other advantages. Where to Buy: $199.99 $159.95 at Amazon $199.99 $159.99 at Best Buy $199.95 $159.95 at B&H Photo Roku Ultra Roku’s latest Ultra streamer has built-in ethernet, a rechargeable voice remote with backlit buttons, and AirPlay 2 support. You can also control it with Amazon Alexa through a compatible smart speaker. The Roku Channel app lets you stream over 400 free live TV stations, plus exclusive movies like Weird: The Al Yankovic Story . Where to Buy: $149.99 $99.99 at Amazon $149.99 $99.99 at Best Buy $149.99 $99.99 at B&H Photo Roku Streaming Stick Plus Roku’s Streaming Stick Plus supports 4K playback and features a slim design, so it won’t block nearby ports. It plugs straight into your TV’s HDMI port and can be powered by your TV’s USB port, so you don’t need an additional plug. It also comes with Roku’s Voice Remote, giving you hands-free control. Where to Buy: $59.99 $34.99 at Amazon $59.99 $34.99 at Walmart $59.99 $34.99 at Best Buy Kindle Colorsoft (16GB) The 16GB Kindle Colorsoft is Amazon’s latest color e-reader. It features a 7-inch 300ppi screen, an adjustable frontlight, and a battery that can last up to eight weeks. Where to Buy: $249.99 $189.99 at Amazon $249.99 $189.99 at Best Buy $249.99 $189.99 at Target Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition The 2024 version of the Paperwhite is steeply discounted, and nearly identical to the latest model. The Signature Edition includes double the storage (to 32GB), no ads, and wireless charging. Read our review. Where to Buy: $199.99 $169.99 at Amazon $199.99 $169.99 at Best Buy $199.99 $169.99 at Target Bose SoundLink Plus While the Max is an awesome, powerful speaker, the Plus packs a ton of performance into a more portable form factor. It has an IP67 rating, and it’s easy to clean, too. Read our review . Where to Buy: $269 $179 at Amazon $269 $179 at Best Buy $269 $179 at Bose Bose SoundLink Max Bose’s SoundLink Max improves on the smaller Flex with true stereo sound — and very powerful sound at that. It’s got a removable handle for easy transport, and there’s an aux input for playing audio when you want to listen at a higher quality than what Bluetooth can deliver. Read our review . Where to Buy: $399 $279 at Amazon $399 $279 at Best Buy $399 $279 at Bose Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 foldable charging dock Slap a recent iPhone onto this charging pad and it’ll charge at fast 25W speeds. It can also charge AirPods, and includes a cord and wall adapter. Where to Buy: $60 $42.99 at Amazon $100 $75 at Amazon (w/ Apple Watch support) Belkin Charging Case for Nintendo Switch 2 The case features an integrated power bank and a small pocket to stow an AirTag (or other similarly sized Bluetooth tracker). Where to Buy: $69.99 $59.49 at Amazon (in black or sand) Asus ProArt 27-inch 1440p USB-C monitor An affordable color-accurate monitor that can easily connect to a MacBook or Windows machine that has USB-C video support. It’s a good price for a fully-featured 1440p monitor. Where to Buy: $299 $275 at Amazon Belkin MagSafe 15W 2-in-1 wireless charging dock A slick 2-in-1 charger that can charge your magnet-friendly iPhone or Pixel at a relatively speedy pace. Its extra charging pad supports AirPods, the Apple Watch, and other Qi-ready accessories. Where to Buy: $120 $59.99 at Amazon Ring Battery Doorbell 2K At more than half-off, the second-gen version is a good deal if you want 2K video and easy installation. However, its battery is built-in, so you’ll need to disconnect the doorbell to charge via USB-C. Where to Buy: $99.99 $39.99 at Amazon $99.99 $39.99 at Best Buy Bissell ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus carpet cleaner Bissell’s Little Green is handy, but doesn’t cut it for big jobs. If you have pets and a lot of carpet to clean, this is one of the most powerful upright carpet cleaners in its price range. Where to Buy: $279.99 $209.99 at Amazon $279.99 $209.99 at Bissell Ring Floodlight Cam 2K This model requires wired power, and provides 2K resolution (with AI tuning) and 6x digital zoom. It’s bright (2,000 lumens), and provides a loud alarm if you need to use it. Where to Buy: $199.99 $99.99 at Amazon Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro The highest-end battery-powered option of the lineup. It can record in 4K with 10x digital zoom, and its battery can be swapped for another as it recharges. Where to Buy: $249.99 $149.99 at Amazon $249.99 $149.99 at Best Buy Amazon Fire HD 8 tablet The eight-inch tablet with lockscreen ads has 4GB RAM (respectable for streaming apps and mobile games), plus 64GB of storage and a microSD slot for viewing locally-stored media. This model doesn’t support Google Play Store, though it’s easy to sideload it. Where to Buy: $129.99 $79.99 at Amazon (4GB RAM, 64GB) $99.99 $54.99 at Best Buy (3GB RAM, 32GB) Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone The X12 OmniCyclone uses AI to identify and blast stains to help ensure they’re properly cleaned with minimal passes. It includes a dock, which empties the vac, washes its rolling mop with heated, pressurized water, and refills its reservoirs. Where to Buy: $1499.99 $799 at Amazon $1499.99 $841.99 at Best Buy $1499.99 $842 at Ecovacs Blink Mini pan and tilt camera The panning and tilting accessory gives the Blink Mini some new powers, including 360-degree control via the Blink app. Also included is the camera, which is usually $25 by itself. Where to Buy: $39.99 $23.99 at Amazon $39.99 $23.99 at Best Buy Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus The latest version of Amazon’s zippy Fire TV Stick 4K streams in 4K resolution, as its name suggests, and features support for Wi-Fi 6, Dolby Atmos / Vision, and HDR10 Plus. Where to Buy: $69.99 $37.99 at Amazon $69.99 $37.99 at Best Buy Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Max (2023, latest model) Amazon’s highest-end streaming stick supports Wi-Fi 6E and offers double the storage of its predecessor. It also displays widgets and artwork when idle, while continuing to offer a terrific selection of streaming apps. Plus, it runs on the new and improved Fire TV OS, which makes it easier to find something to watch. Where to Buy: $84.99 $44.99 at Amazon $84.99 $44.99 at Best Buy Amazon Fire TV Cube (2022, latest model) The hybrid Echo and Fire TV is faster than its predecessor with extensive hands-free voice control capabilities, support for Wi-Fi 6E, and excellent performance. Read our review . Where to Buy: $199.99 $89.99 at Amazon $199.99 $89.99 at Best Buy Amazon Echo Spot Amazon’s smart speaker-meets-alarm clock has a 2.83-inch squared-off display for showing the time, weather, album art, and other bits of info you may want at your bedside. Unlike the original, there’s no camera to worry about having in your bedroom — though it does have a mutable mic for Alexa voice controls. Read our review. Where to Buy: $109.99 $54.99 at Amazon $109.99 $54.99 at Best Buy $109.99 $54.99 at Target Amazon Echo Dot Max The Echo Dot Max is an elegant redesign of Amazon’s orb-shaped smart speaker, with high-quality knit fabric, a flat face, a new LED ring, and touch controls. It’s the first Echo Dot with Amazon’s improved two-way speaker system and support for its new AI-powered assistant, Alexa Plus, which is enabled out of the box. Where to Buy: $119.99 $79.99 at Amazon $119.99 $79.99 at Best Buy $119.99 $79.99 at Target Amazon Echo Dot (Fifth-Gen) Amazon’s Echo Dot is an affordable way to add a smart speaker to your space. The small, powerful speaker offers surprisingly robust sound, and it’s great for controlling smart home devices, including those compatible with Matter. The Dot also offers faster response times than its predecessor, and it can act as an extender for an Eero Wi-Fi system. Read our review . Where to Buy: $79.99 $39.99 at Amazon $79.99 $39.99 at Best Buy $79.99 $39.99 at Target Amazon Echo Show 11 (2025) The Echo Show 11 features an 11-inch screen and 1080p resolution. It includes Alexa Plus and can be used as a smart home hub with support Thread, Matter, and Zigbee smart home protocols. Read our review. Where to Buy: $249.99 $149.99 at Amazon $249.99 $149.99 at Best Buy $249.99 $149.99 at Target Amazon Echo Show 15 The new year is the perfect time to reset your routines and get organized, and the Echo Show 15 is a great tool for doing just that. Designed to function as a shared household hub, it keeps calendars, schedules, reminders, to-do lists, and notes visible at a glance, making it easier to keep on top of things. As an Alexa-enabled smart display, you can also add events by voice and control compatible smart home devices. Where to Buy: $349.99 $249.99 at Amazon $349.99 $249.99 at Best Buy $349.99 $249.99 at Target Eero Pro 6E tri-band router Eero’s Pro 6E mesh router is the Amazon-owned company’s last-gen model. It supports the 6GHz Wi-Fi band with speeds of up to 1.3Gbps and covers up to 2,000 square feet with one unit. Wired speeds can go up to 2.5Gbps. Read our review . Where to Buy: $199.99 $149.99 at Amazon (single pack) $499.99 $374.99 at Best Buy (three-pack) $499.99 $374.99 at Amazon (three-pack) Samsung 32-inch Movingstyle smart display Similar to LG’s rollable StanbyME display, the Movingstyle Essential is a 32-inch 4K display on a base that’s height-adjustable (and supports swiveling, pivoting and tilting). Unlike LG’s model, though, this one has no built-in battery. Where to Buy: $699.99 $499.99 at Amazon Dreame X50 Ultra With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum and mop hybrid. Where to Buy: $1099.99 $899.99 at Amazon (for Prime members) $1099.99 $849.99 at Dreame (with free account)

raw_title: Lanterns Season 1 Finale Review & Recap
title: Lanterns Season 1 Finale Review & Recap
raw_summary: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 8! How much you enjoy the finale of Lanterns Season 1 is going to depend heavily on how well you can manage your expectations. There have been plenty of outlandish fan theories regarding where the series has been building towards and the identity of Hal Jordan’s killer. Is Hal even dead, or is this all part of some massive conspiracy involving complex doppelganger constructs or Manhunter-based resurrection? Well, it’s best to put all of that to the side and just enjoy the finale for what it is. It’s probably not going to shock most of us with its plot twists and character developments. Nor does it represent a pivot back to the sort of spectacle we saw in Episode 5. But it does deliver an ending that feels true to the story the series has been telling all along. A lot of burning questions have been hanging over the series in light of Episode 7, which changed the game by dragging John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and the Halogram to a war-ravaged alien world and inserting Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) back into the mix. Is this where the series blows the doors wide open in terms of the cosmic Green Lantern elements? Is Sinestro himself, not the mysteries in Rushville, the ultimate endgame of Season 1? No, not really. The fact that Episode 8 opens with a quiet flashback to 2016 and then to Hal’s life immediately after being released from prison clues us into the fact that this is still a small-town murder mystery at its core. Even when the focus does shift to Sinestro and the gang, Sinestro himself is more a means of exposition than a supervillain mastermind. These early scenes wind up resolving a number of the show’s ongoing mysteries. We learn that Noah (Shea Pritchard) is indeed a Manhunter of sorts. He was the one who busted Sinestro out of Spazkaban, all for the purpose of forging a Lantern Noah can use to slaughter the Guardians. Everything is wrapped up in a neat little package. Mostly. Part of me is disappointed that Sinestro's ultimate role in the series is so minimal. He’s the Green Lantern villain, after all, but we only see him in a handful of scenes this season, one of which involves him being waterboarded by John. The series never fully leaned into the possibilities of Sinestro as the Hannibal Lecter to Hal’s Will Graham. Worse, perhaps, is that his comments about the value of fear as a weapon suggest that there’s no real history of Sinestro forming his own Lantern Corps in the DCU. Maybe we’ll get there in a future season, but probably not with Hal in the picture. Like with Hector Hammond (Jason Manuel Olazábal), it feels like the series has really downplayed Sinestro’s importance in Hal’s own story. That all being said, the Noah of it all works well for me. No, the Manhunter reveal is not the most surprising direction the series could have taken. But as Christopher Nolan would argue , just because we can predict a plot twist ahead of time, that doesn’t automatically invalidate the story. Sometimes you just have to let these things play out as they should. The same goes for the later reveal that Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) is Hal’s actual killer. I think most of us saw that one coming, but it makes too much sense not to go down that road. She’s a character who’s been deceiving Hal and John from the very first episode. Not out of malice, but a desire to protect those two alien beings she loves so dearly. For all the ambitious theorizing surrounding Hal’s murder, it feels appropriate that the whole thing boils down to a momentary burst of passion. And you really can’t fault Macdonald’s performance in this episode, particularly during her tearful confession to John. The same goes for Pierre, who’s given an awful lot of meaty material to work with in the finale. Early on, John is quietly wracked with uncertainty and dread regarding the revelations about Noah. As the episode unfolds, he becomes a man at peace with himself and his place in the cosmos. Through it all, Pierre remains a master of saying a lot through subtle facial expressions and body language. I’ve said it before, but this is a role that could easily have been boring in the wrong hands. Pierre’s are clearly the right hands. Most satisfying of all is the way this episode caps off the season-long tension between John and Hal and shows us the all-important passing of the torch. The Halogram is able to express emotions the real Hal never could, allowing us to appreciate a bond the latter would never be caught dead acknowledging. Hal saying “I love you too, Junior,” is almost hokey, but Kyle Chandler sells the scene so well you simply have to believe it. Read Last Week's Lanterns Review Lanterns Season 1, Episode 7: "The Jordan Boys' Legacy" Granted, I am disappointed the finale doesn’t find a way to keep Chandler in the picture, either by preserving the Halogram or somehow resurrecting the real Hal (something Sinestro seems to believe is possible). It’s tough to imagine a second season of Lanterns working half as well without that critical dynamic between Hal and John. But I suppose that’s a problem for another day. For now, this farewell really tugs at the heartstrings. What we’re left with is a mostly cohesive and satisfying account of how John Stewart finally embraces his destiny as Earth’s Green Lantern. I do think the show could have done a slightly better job of exploring how John has learned to embrace fear rather than push it away. His arc has been more focused on overcoming his conditioning. However, that’s more an issue with the season as a whole rather than this episode in particular. And in any case, the final scenes do a great job of setting him up for bigger and better things in the DCU. At long last, it’s time for John Stewart to fly.

raw_title: Mighty Mike Plays Dad Says He Owns 'Like 12 Companies,' Promises Refunds for AI Shirts
title: Mighty Mike Plays Dad Says He Owns 'Like 12 Companies,' Promises Refunds for AI Shirts
raw_summary: Mighty Mike Plays dad Dave has promised refunds and issued a lengthy explanation after the internet demanded more information about the YouTube ads allegedly purchased by his son and the drama that followed. The Mighty Mike Plays saga began when a father took to YouTube to announce that his son had allegedly used his company credit card to purchase more than $118,000 in video ads. It was a painful and highly relatable story that snowballed into a full-fledged internet spectacle when pricey AI-generated T-shirts and questionable details led many online to look for concrete answers. The controversial father figure came clean in a new video titled " Allow me to Explain " that was uploaded to the Mighty Mike Plays channel last week (via Dexerto ). Dave started the hour-long explainer – which has since been deleted and re-uploaded on a new YouTube channel called Coffee Time with Dave – promising that everyone who purchased one of those T-shirts would receive a refund. “this might be the end of Mighty Mike Plays…” is the funniest thing you could say in front of your dad after putting him 118k in debt and getting him fired — Mako Fukasame 🦈👩‍🏫 | Vershion AU (@MakoFukasame) September 15, 2026 "Dave here. A.k.a. Devoted Dave. A.k.a. Dazzling Dave. A.k.a. Dependable Dave, and the list goes on," Dave said. "I want to give you guys an update: First off, I'm going to say that everyone that got a shirt got refunded whether they asked for it or not. So, whether you wanted a refund or not, you got it." The full video covers allegations related to the Mighty Mike Plays drama and also covers a lot that has nothing to do with it at all. Dave's headline he wants to share, though, is that this all blew up so much faster and so much bigger than he ever expected it to be. He explained that he thought he was simply "venting" about his son's spending with a story that sounds like the kind of thing you'd tell a friend at a bar. Millions of views and a sea of video responses later, and it's clear it didn't pan out the way he ever imagined it would. "I remember thinking, like, you know, I wonder if this video will hit 10,000 views," he said. "That's kind of where I thought it would cap. I didn't think it would go so viral. Everything happened real-time, organically, and I obviously didn't handle everything the right way, essentially, but just to make it clear: I didn't come to YouTube to ask for help. I wasn't looking for any sort of help." Part of the reason why the internet gathered with Minecraft fans to help out is because Dave said the $118,000 hole his son put in his company card resulted in him being fired. He also stated he had just 30 days to make up for the missing money, but in the new video, Dave has clarified some of those details. Instead of losing his job, Dave suggested he technically was not fired in a traditional sense, with that part of the story being a "simplified version" of what actually happened. The reality, he said, is that "the contract between company A and company B just got terminated," adding, "isn't that the same thing?" As many had suspected, he doesn't just own his own company – he owns 12. "Yeah, I own my own company. So what?" Dave clarified. "In fact, you guys didn't even see – I have like 12 companies. Not all of them are productive, as we speak. Some of them are just collecting dust, and just because someone has a company or is a CEO doesn't mean that, 'Oh, OK. Just by having those titles you're actually conducting a profitable business.'" He continued: "But just to clarify, I consider that being fired. If my company lost a contract with this important company, then, I mean, how is that not being fired? Fine. I'll be more specific next time." As for those controversial T-shirts and why he's issuing refunds, Dave said he "didn't want to sit around and let these actual scammers sell people who wanted to be involved in this story." His plan for an official merch page, which allegedly put him "another $10K in the hole," still drew much ire from the internet, at least partially due to its prolific use of AI-generated designs. He explained why he's issued refunds – even if not all that many people found something to buy. "In retrospect, was AI and the merch the way to go? Was the price the way to go? No," he said. "Look, I'm going to admit when I was wrong: That was not the move. I shouldn't have used AI. Although, at the time, I know I defended it. There is a now-infamous deleted post, which I crashed out." He later added: "I do agree now, and if I could go back, I'd do it differently, but again, I didn't have the luxury of time. Time was running out. We had to figure something out, so yeah, I had AI create some designs. I still feel like those designs were flawless, gorgeous, beautiful, superb, and there is about 100 people who got free shirts." It's unclear if Dave's explanation video will be enough to satisfy the many online who looked into the Minecraft YouTube channel after the events surrounding it kicked off last month. If this is the first time you're hearing of Mighty Mike Plays and the drama surrounding AI-generated T-shirt designs, there's no need to fear. We broke down everything you could ever want to know about the story right here .

raw_title: Blindfolded Tekken 8 Player Achieves One of the Game’s Top Ranks from Beginner
title: Blindfolded Tekken 8 Player Achieves One of the Game’s Top Ranks from Beginner
raw_summary: Professional Tekken 8 player SuperBrine is going viral after reaching God of Destruction using Alisa while completely blindfolded with a sleep mask. SuperBrine has been streaming his run on Twitch in the form of seven separate broadcasts, starting in June 2026 . The final stream from this series, broadcast in early October , has become a hot topic within the fighting game community, as he was able to reach one of the game’s top ranks from Beginner while obscuring his vision with a sleep mask. It’s an impressive feat no matter how you swing it, standing as a testament to SuperBrine’s skill as a player and Tekken 8’s laudable sound design — but, perhaps unsurprisingly, his blindfolded run from Beginner to God of Destruction has sparked no end of debate about the game's difficulty and Alisa’s ease of use as a character. HERE WE ARE... First person ever to get From BEGINNER to GoD rank 100% Blindfolded on LIVE stream This took me alot of effort and time, but hell yea worth it. my whole run from the beginning to the end is SAVED in my twitch highlights. a new youtube video incoming #TEKKEN8 https://t.co/JhEpwWijjw — SuperBrine (@SuperBrineTK) October 4, 2026 I got the chance to sit down with SuperBrine to discuss his self-imposed challenge and find out if it was legit or not. He confirmed that there was no way he was able to see through the sleep mask (which are typically made out of thick material with dense cushions on the eyes), and reiterated that he’d streamed his entire run live on Twitch for all to see, so there was no way for him to cheat. As for the ‘why’ of it all, SuperBrine said he wanted to prove that he could do something impossible, and is hopeful the challenge will help boost his visibility as a pro player. He also admitted that this undertaking was not, in any way, meant as a criticism of Tekken 8 as a game, despite the discourse surrounding his efforts on social media. “My primary goal was simply to take on a challenge that most people will consider impossible and prove that I can do it,” he said. “I want to clarify that I didn't do this to criticize the game or suggest that it's poorly designed in any way. It's actually the exact opposite. I genuinely love this game, and I thrive on pushing my own personal limits through these kinds of extreme challenges. I am deeply passionate about it, and since my long-term plan is to pursue competing as my professional career, these kinds of challenges will directly support my career." Outside of being unable to see, SuperBrine revealed that the hardest part of this challenge was that his eyes began to burn from being closed so long beneath the sleep mask. This, on top of being mentally drained from putting so much effort into the task, forced him to take frequent breaks. “The physical toll was actually surprising. …Mentally, it required extreme patience, without it, completing this run simply wouldn't be possible,” he said. Even a top player would have difficulty on ranked if blindfolded, so how did SuperBrine manage to pull it off? He told me that he relied on his foundational skills as a fighting game player and a keen sense of how people play on different ranks, as well as Tekken 8's helpful sound cues. “It comes down to a massive amount of foundational experience. Playing on multiple smurf accounts over time gave me an exact read on the game knowledge players have at different ranks. Because of that, I knew precisely which strings and flowcharts would work and which wouldn't. Beyond that, precise hearing is crucial. You would be able to instantly differentiate specific sounds knowing whether a move resulted in a wall splat or not, if it was a hit or a block, and if you landed a counter hit versus a normal hit. Ultimately, it’s all about paying attention to the audio and knowing exactly the type of player you are facing," he explained. For those who believe that Tekken 8 is so easy that anyone can pick up a blindfold and a controller and get to God of Destruction, SuperBrine invites you to try it; but it’s not that simple, because if it was, anyone would be able to do it. “People are free to have their own opinions on it. There will always be positive and negative ones, and I respect that. But turning this into a criticism of Tekken 8 will not help the future of the game. You can't reach God of Destruction blindfolded just by picking a specific character and hoping for the best. It takes thousands of hours of game knowledge, knowing what kind of players you will face and what level of game knowledge they have, and relying entirely on audio cues. If it was just a flaw in the game or an easy character, someone else would have done it already,” he said. SuperBrine chose to give himself this challenge; there are many other fighting game players who have reached top ranks and even become pros in spite of having actual disabilities. For instance, the late great BrolyLegs was a top Street Fighter player who could duke it out with the best of them using only his mouth to move his controller. And BlindWarriorSven, a blind Street Fighter 6 player who lost his eyesight at six years old due to cancer, won a livestreamed set at Evo 2-1 with E. Honda thanks the game’s impressive accessibility features that allowed him to 'hear' where his opponent was at on-screen.
